verdict.root_cause: Platform automation halved the frontend workload's CPU ceiling (limits.cpu 1 -> 500m, request raised to match) about seven minutes before onset [tr_ec5e968a606a]. The edit recreated the pod: a full cold-start sequence appears at 21:10:11, one second after the change, with all five downstream gRPC clients connecting cleanly [tr_44133780e673]. From that point the frontend goes quiet — no further log output [tr_44133780e673], zero error spans across 22 samples [tr_a1e1555af34a, tr_d2052c256486], and three intervals with no spans at all, meaning it served nothing in those intervals [tr_a1e1555af34a, tr_d2052c256486]. That is CPU starvation under the new ceiling: requests stall rather than fail, so callers hang while the frontend reports no errors. The limit edit is how it started; exhaustion is the failing mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: The only substantive change in the window is a CPU ceiling cut on the frontend itself; no image, version or flag change exists [tr_ec5e968a606a]. The restart timestamp matches the edit to the second and shows healthy service discovery and five successful downstream connections [tr_44133780e673], which argues against a wrong address, credential or dependency as the mechanism. The post-restart signature is absence rather than failure: flat-zero error ratio with zero variance plus intervals containing no spans at all [tr_a1e1555af34a, tr_d2052c256486] and silent logs [tr_44133780e673] — work not completing while nothing errors is what throttling looks like from outside the container. The downstream story is weak: the nine CheckAvailability failures are a single-second burst at 21:10:03, before the alert, and never recur [tr_44133780e673], while reservation logged no CheckAvailability activity at all [tr_eacfd29a4cab]. Traces could have arbitrated but returned nothing for frontend across the whole window including the healthy period, so the trace path is itself impaired [tr_adf228881c31]. The fix is restoring the previous CPU limit.
open_questions: No container-level data was ever returned — CPU throttling ratio, restart counts and OOM/eviction events were requested but absent [tr_d2052c256486]; throttling is inferred, not measured.

Why frontend traces are missing for the entire window including the pre-incident baseline, and why a zero-result query was flagged truncated [tr_adf228881c31] — a broken telemetry pipeline would undermine the 'no spans means no traffic' inference.
What the 21:10:03 CheckAvailability burst actually hit; the log line carries no peer or status code and reservation's logs are empty under that filter [tr_44133780e673, tr_eacfd29a4cab].

alternatives.root_cause: The frontend telemetry pipeline is broken and the apparent outage is an observability gap rather than a service fault.
alternatives.why_not: It does not explain the alert at 21:17:39, and a concrete CPU-limit cut landing seven minutes before onset is a better fit than instrument failure [tr_ec5e968a606a].

alternatives.root_cause: A downstream dependency behind the search/availability path became slow, and the frontend hung waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: The only evidence is a single-second error burst before onset that never recurs [tr_44133780e673]; no trace or metric data identifies a slow downstream, and reservation's logs are empty [tr_eacfd29a4cab, tr_adf228881c31].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring frontend's prior resource config (limits.cpu 1 / requests.cpu 100m, undoing the 500m/500m edit at 21:10:10 [tr_ec5e968a606a]) and recreating the container should let frontend complete requests again. Observable as: the frontend span rate denominator becoming defined and non-zero in every 5m interval (no repeat of the three no-span intervals), and the frontend Loki stream emitting request lines beyond a single cold-start block instead of going silent as it did after 21:10:11.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, 10 minutes after the revert and its cold start, frontend span rate is still undefined/zero and Loki still shows nothing past the startup block. Note two live doubts: container-level throttling, restart and OOM data were never returned [tr_d2052c256486], so starvation is inferred not measured; and Tempo returned nothing for the whole window with a truncated flag [tr_adf228881c31], so if logs show traffic while span metrics stay empty, suspect the telemetry pipeline rather than a failed fix.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong this is a wasted recreate of the alerted user-facing service, dropping in-flight requests and its in-process cache. Restoring a 1-core ceiling also lets frontend push more load downstream; if the real fault is a saturated dependency, this deepens it. It also reverses a platform-automation action, which may be re-applied and flap unless that automation is paused.
proposal.blast_radius: frontend is recreated: external callers see resets for the restart duration. Its five downstream dependencies (profile, recommendation, reservation, search, user) see traffic stop, then resume at possibly higher volume.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on the user-facing frontend with no open incidents to attribute it to cannot be dismissed. Only the seed alerted, so the cause could be local to frontend or an unmeasured downstream dependency; no fault class is suggested yet.
